emissionSites.emissionDescription: emitToolInvocationFunctions() (lines 36-73) emits one async invoke<Tool>Tool function per tool name, each containing THREE throws in its template literal: line 48 `throw new TypeError(descriptor.describeToolArgs())` (input parse failure), lines 54-56 `throw new TypeError(DOCUMENTED_ERROR_PREFIX + String(invokeResult.httpStatus), { cause: ... })` (HTTP >= 400), lines 60-66 `throw new TypeError('Output validation error: ' + validation.message, { cause: ... })` (output validation failure). Plus two fixed-string throws in the file body: line 108 `throw new TypeError('Unknown tool: ' + String(name))` in invokeToolByName switch default, and line 139 same string in callToolWithValidation isToolName guard. Output: 24 invocation functions x 3 + 2 fixed = 74 throws in runtime/execute.ts.
emissionSites.fixApproach: Change the emitted invoke<Tool>Tool functions to return a Result instead of throwing: emit `return err({ kind: 'input-validation', message: descriptor.describeToolArgs() })`, `return err({ kind: 'http-error', httpStatus, payload })`, and `return err({ kind: 'output-validation', message, issues, attemptedStatuses })`, and on success `return ok({ status, data })`. Change the emitted return type from `Promise<ToolResultForName<...>>` to `Promise<Result<ToolResultForName<...>, ToolCallError>>` (or a generated ToolCallError discriminated union), import `ok`/`err`/`Result` from @oaknational/result, and propagate Result through invokeToolByName/callTool/callToolWithValidation overloads. The two 'Unknown tool' guards become `return err({ kind: 'unknown-tool', name })`. Define ToolCallError once in the runtime contract and have callers pattern-match instead of try/catch.

emissionSites.emissionDescription: buildExports() emits the per-tool descriptor file body (one tools/<tool>.ts per tool). FOUR throws are emitted into each tool file via the lines[] template: line 72 `throw new TypeError('Missing response descriptor for documented status <N> on <operationId>.')` (module-load guard), line 97 `throw new TypeError(describeToolArgs())` inside the descriptor.invoke closure (input parse failure), line 102 `throw new TypeError('Invalid method on endpoint: <METHOD> for <path>')` (missing client method), line 109 `throw new UndocumentedResponseError(status, '<operationId>', documentedStatuses, responseBody)` (no descriptor for HTTP status). emit-index.ts is reached via generate-tool-file.ts -> emitters.ts -> emitIndex(). Output: 23 tool files x 4 = 92 throws across mcp-tools/tools/*.ts.
emissionSites.fixApproach: The line-72 module-load guard is a generator-time invariant about the response map and can remain a thrown TypeError at import time (it is not a per-call failure path) OR be eliminated by asserting it at generate time. The three per-call throws inside descriptor.invoke (lines 97, 102, 109) should instead make invoke return a Result-typed payload: emit `return err({ kind: 'input-validation', ... })`, `return err({ kind: 'invalid-method', method, path })`, and for the undocumented-response case emit `return err({ kind: 'undocumented-response', status, operationId, documentedStatuses, responseBody })` rather than `throw new UndocumentedResponseError(...)`. Change the emitted invoke signature to return `Promise<Result<{ httpStatus; payload }, ...>>` and update the ToolDescriptor contract type (contract/tool-descriptor.contract.ts) accordingly. UndocumentedResponseError stays as the error value carried inside err(), not thrown. The execute-file generator (above) then consumes the Result rather than relying on a throw.

emissionSites.emissionDescription: emitResponseValidators() emits the response-map.ts helper functions block (template string at lines 66-123) containing FIVE fixed-string throws: line 71 `throw new TypeError('No response schema for id: ' + String(id))` (getResponseRecord), line 79 same string (requireSchema void-source guard), line 101 `throw new TypeError('Invalid id: ' + String(key))` (getResponseSchemaByOperationIdAndStatus), line 113 `throw new TypeError('Invalid operationId: ' + String(operationId))` (getResponseSchemaByPathAndMethodAndStatus), line 119 `throw new TypeError('Method not allowed for path: ' + String(method) + ' ' + String(path))` (getResponseSchemaForEndpoint). These 5 helper throws account for response-map.ts output lines 1331/1339/1361/1373/1379.
emissionSites.fixApproach: Change the emitted helper functions to return `Result<CurriculumSchemaDefinition, ResponseMapError>` instead of throwing: getResponseRecord/requireSchema/getResponseSchemaByOperationIdAndStatus/getResponseSchemaByPathAndMethodAndStatus/getResponseSchemaForEndpoint each emit `return err({ kind: '...' })` and `return ok(schema)`. Update the emitted return-type annotations in the template and propagate Result through callers (the tool descriptor build and cross-validation consumers). For the latent void-entry IIFE in buildSchemaExpression (line 162), replace the throwing IIFE with a sentinel value/typed Err so void responses surface as a Result rather than crashing at field access. Import ok/err/Result from @oaknational/result in the emitted header.

emissionSites.fixApproach: Change the three emitted accessor functions (getToolEntryFromToolName, getToolNameFromOperationId, getOperationIdFromToolName) to return Result: emit `return err({ kind: 'unknown-tool', toolName })` / `return err({ kind: 'unknown-operation', operationId })` and `return ok(entry/toolName/operationId)`. Callers (notably the emitted execute.ts which calls getToolEntryFromToolName and getToolFromToolName) must thread the Result. The generator-side line-40 throw stays as a build-time invariant (acceptable: codegen fail-fast, not runtime).

emissionSites.emissionDescription: buildResponseDescriptorHelpers() emits the response-map.ts descriptorsByOperationId tail (template lines 68-82). ONE fixed-string throw at template line 78: `throw new TypeError('No response descriptors for operationId: ' + String(operationId))` inside getResponseDescriptorsByOperationId. Maps to response-map.ts output line 1903. This function is imported and called by every emitted tool file (emit-index.ts line 56 emits `getResponseDescriptorsByOperationId(operationId)`).
emissionSites.fixApproach: Emit `return err({ kind: 'unknown-operation-id', operationId })` and `return ok(record)`; change emitted return type to `Result<Readonly<Record<string, ResponseDescriptorRecord>>, ...>`. Recommend keeping load-time guards as throws and converting only the per-request paths; this site is load-time so it may legitimately stay thrown.

notes: Reconciliation: traced output throws sum to exactly 185 across the on-disk generated files (execute.ts 74, tools/*.ts 92 across 23 files x 4, response-map.ts 6 = 5 helper + 1 descriptor-helper, path-parameters.ts 4, definitions.ts 3, routing/url-helpers.ts 2, ground-truths lesson-slugs-by-subject.ts 2, observability/zero-hit-fixtures.ts 1, search/fixtures.ts 1). The prompt's ~189/187 estimate is ~2-4 high versus the current generated tree; the live count is 185. The discrepancy is most plausibly a tool-file count drift (worklist assumed ~96 in tools/*.ts; actual is 92 across 23 files) partly offset by other rounding.

execute.ts arithmetic: grep shows 24 (not 25) tool invocation functions each emitting 3 throws = 72, plus 2 fixed 'Unknown tool' throws = 74. The generate-execute-file.ts generator emits one function per tool name in the sorted names array; the build also emits callTool overloads (no throws).
tools/*.ts: 23 generated tool files (excluding tests), each emitting exactly 4 throws from emit-index.ts buildExports = 92. Verified one example (get-subjects.ts: lines 51/76/81/88).

Generator-side vs emitted: clusters.json buckets c16/c17 ('generator-source') and c18 ('scripts') are throws in the GENERATOR'S OWN code that run at codegen time (e.g. generate-definitions-file.ts line 40 'No operation id found for tool'), NOT emitted into generated output. Those are out of scope for this trace (they are real source throws, fixable on their own merits as build-time invariants). This report covers ONLY templates/statements that EMIT a throw into generated output.

The response-map void-entry IIFE in emit-response-validators.ts buildSchemaExpression (line 162) is a latent emission site: it would emit `(() => { throw new TypeError(...); })()` per void-source response entry, but the current OpenAPI schema yields zero void entries, so it contributes 0 today. Worth fixing in the same pass to prevent future regressions.

Result pattern is already available at packages/core/result (@oaknational/result) exporting Result/Ok/Err/ok/err/isOk/isErr/map/flatMap etc. The use-result-pattern rule applies. The cleanest fix threads a generated discriminated-union error type (ToolCallError / ResponseMapError / PathParamError / OakUrlError / FixtureError) through the emitted return types and updates the ToolDescriptor contract (contract/tool-descriptor.contract.ts) plus the runtime callers; UndocumentedResponseError becomes an error VALUE carried in err(), not thrown.

UndocumentedResponseError and tool-descriptor.contract.ts are themselves GENERATED runtime-contract files (banner 'GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT') but contain zero throws, so they are not in the worklist; however the contract type DEFINITION must change (emit Result-returning invoke signature) as part of the emit-index.ts and generate-execute-file.ts fixes -- locate their generator templates (contract emission) before editing.

Load-time vs request-time distinction: several emitted throws are module-load invariants over generator-controlled data (emit-index.ts line 72 'Missing response descriptor', build-response-descriptor-helpers.ts line 78, the ground-truths/fixtures parse guards). These are defensible as fail-fast build/load assertions and may legitimately remain throws if the owner scopes the no-throw rule to per-request runtime paths only. The clearly request-path throws that MUST become Result: execute.ts per-call throws (input/http/output validation), emit-index invoke per-call throws (input/method/undocumented-response), and all the response-map/path-parameters/url-helpers lookup helpers that run per request.
